ai.title: CLI auth retry logic switches to HTTP status codes
ai.summary: CLI auth and error handling now derive retryability from HTTP status codes via `isRetryableStatusCode` and `getErrorStatusCode` instead of custom `NetworkError` classes and `RETRYABLE_ERROR_CODES`. SDK retry config removed from `createRunConfig`; auth status logic in `app.tsx` updated to handle 4xx as 'ok' and 5xx/retryable as 'retrying'/'unreachable'. `send-message.ts` simplifies out-of-credits handling using `OUT_OF_CREDITS_MESSAGE`. Covers CLI auth, message sending, and error utils.

eli5.text: When the CLI has trouble reaching the server, it now decides whether to keep trying based on standard web response codes (like 408 for timeouts, 429 for rate limits, and 5xx for server errors) instead of a custom error tracking system. This means the login check and message sending will show you a clearer status: 'retrying' when it can try again, or 'unreachable' when there's no point continuing, and you'll get one consistent message if you run out of credits. The change is live today for anyone using the CLI tool. What you'd notice is that errors during login or sending messages behave more predictably and the prompts guiding you to fix issues (like adding credits) appear consistently.

ai.title: CLI out-of-credits banner with live polling and Enter-to-buy flow
ai.summary: New `outOfCredits` input mode replaces `usage` on credit exhaustion, rendering `OutOfCreditsBanner` instead of the standard input bar. Banner polls `useUsageQuery` every 5s, gates restoration behind a `confirmedZeroBalance` check to prevent stale-cache false positives, and exposes a global `areCreditsRestored` flag. `Enter` triggers `open(WEBSITE_URL + '/usage')` unless credits already restored, in which case it resets to `default` mode; `Escape` or `Ctrl+C` exits the mode. Covers `cli/src/components/out-of-credits-banner.tsx`, `chat.tsx`, `chat-input-bar.tsx`, `send-message.ts`, `use-chat-keyboard.ts`, `input-modes.ts`, `keyboard-actions.ts`.

eli5.text: When you run out of AI credits in the command-line tool, you now get a dedicated screen that replaces the normal text input area, showing a friendly message that your credits are gone and automatically checking every 5 seconds whether your balance has been restored. While on that screen, pressing Enter opens your web browser directly to the credits page where you can buy more, unless the tool has already detected that credits are back, then it quietly switches you back to normal chat without needing to buy anything. The Escape key or Ctrl+C still exits the screen so you can walk away at any time. This only affects people using the command-line version of the assistant.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.568 ships auth retry, out-of-credits banner, and 402
ai.summary: This release bumps the Freebuff CLI to 1.0.568, publishing three same-day improvements to the `cli/` package surface. Auth error handling now derives retryability from HTTP status codes rather than custom NetworkError classes, the payment-required path detects HTTP 402 via AI SDK APICallError duck typing, and credit exhaustion swaps the usage input mode for a live-polling OutOfCreditsBanner with an Enter-to-buy flow. These changes consolidate CLI auth, message sending, error utils, and the agent runtime step runner into a status-code-driven retry and billing-error model.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies only `cli/release/package.json`, changing the `version` field from 1.0.567 to 1.0.568. No functional code changes are present in this commit; the surrounding same-day release history (auth retry via HTTP status codes, out-of-credits banner with live polling, payment-required detection via HTTP 402) is documented in the analysis notes as the content of release 1.0.568.

eli5.text: This release makes the CLI smarter about handling payment problems and running out of credits. When you hit a paywall or run out of free credits, the app now shows a clear out-of-credits banner that tells you what to do and lets you press Enter to fix it, instead of getting stuck. It also better detects when a service is asking for payment (HTTP 402 status) so it can respond the right way. The retry system now looks at standard web error codes to decide if something is worth trying again, making authentication and messaging more reliable. Upgrading means fewer confusing errors and a smoother experience when your account needs attention.

ai.title: Fix send-message test assertion for payment error input mode
ai.summary: Updated `send-message.test.ts` assertion to expect `setInputModeMock` called with `'outOfCredits'` instead of `'usage'`. Aligns test with current implementation handling payment errors. Internal test fix only.

eli5.text: When you run out of credits while using the CLI, the tool now correctly switches the input mode to the out-of-credits screen instead of the generic usage screen. In the test that checks this behavior, the assertion was updated to expect the correct mode name. This is a behind-the-scenes fix to keep the tests accurate and working with the current implementation.
